_meta.description: Which diff-review criteria are correctness and which are process (#3907). A non-pass finding on a correctness criterion is a defect report: under a warn verdict, /work Step 4g and the Merge-Back Review Gate Tier 3 run the one fix cycle before admitting, and file a bug through file-issue.js only when the fix is not achievable. A warn whose non-pass findings are all on process criteria is admitted as before. A criterion this file does not list is treated as correctness and named unclassified in the run report, so a criterion added upstream is fixed first until someone classifies it.
consumers: .claude/scripts/shared/lib/issue-duplicates.js (codeReviewCategories — /code-review Step 8 matches a finding to a bug the gate filed)
_meta.criteriaSource: .claude/skills/diff-review/review-criteria.json — every criterion id there is classified here (tests/scripts/shared/lib/merge-back-gate.test.js)

criteria.reason: An error path that ends in the wrong outcome is a behavior defect.
Unhandled edge input is a behavior defect (#3886, #3905 were merged as warns of this kind).
A path that escapes its root is a security defect.
State that composes wrongly across calls is a behavior defect.
A broken contract with an external tool or format is a behavior defect.
A counterpart left on the old behavior is a behavior defect (diff-review 1.3.0).
A change that can stop halfway or interleave leaves inconsistent state, a behavior defect (diff-review 1.3.0).
An unbounded call in a time-limited context can exhaust its caller's budget, a behavior defect (diff-review 1.3.0).
A security fault is a defect, whatever severity the reviewer gave it.
Attribution of work to ACs, not behavior.
Scope bookkeeping; Tier 1's scope-drift check owns the hard gate.
Test presence is a process check; a missing test is not itself a defect in behavior.
Commit attribution; Tier 1 owns the hard gate.
